title: First 72h Command Pad: launch-day KPIs & tactical checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is the compact command pad for the first 72 hours after a product ops launch window. Designed to be a single-pane-of-glass working doc for on-call leads, product ops, SRE, support triage, and the comms lead. Use this doc during the launch window and convert into the postmortem seed afterwards.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to staged feature launches (small cohort -> phased rollout) and beta toggles for Hosted API features.
- Assumes preflight checks completed (see preflight checklist link in linked_artifacts).
- Focus: measurable KPIs, immediate mitigations, and communication playbook for 0–72h.

High-level timeline (working):
- T0 (go/no-go): 0h — traffic shift begins, feature toggles flip, canaries enabled
- T0+0–6h: immediate smoke validation and critical alerts window
- T0+6–24h: stability triage, rolling metrics review, early adopters feedback
- T0+24–72h: capacity/latency tuning, incident remediation, ramp decision for wider rollout

Owners (quick roster):
- Command lead: Marisol Duarte (product-ops) — overall decisions, go/no-go calls
- SRE lead: Ethan Park — infra, autoscaling, latency SLOs
- Serving runtime lead: Ravi Singh — model variants, fallback rules, batching configs
- CS/Support lead: Priya Nambiar — customer comms, priority support routing
- Comms & Docs: Sofie Larsson — public status updates, internal briefing notes
- Oncall escalation: pager rotation as per SRE rota (ops-oncall@redwood.ai)

Critical KPIs to monitor (single-line thresholds + immediate action):
1) 99th pct latency (generation) — baseline: <= 1.1s; warn at +50% (~>1.65s); critical at +100% (~>2.2s).
   - Action: toggle to lower-capacity model variant or enable burst-capacity routing.
2) Error rate (5m window, client-visible) — baseline: <0.3%; warn >= 1%; critical >= 3%.
   - Action: roll back to previous stable model version, enable automatic fallback.
3) Token throughput (tokens/sec cluster) — expected ramp curve in runbook; deviation >25% below expected triggers autoscale review.
   - Action: adjust pod counts, enable reserved capacity nodes.
4) Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV cache) — expected >= 40% for cohort; drop below 20% indicates misrouting or cache warming problem.
   - Action: flush or rebuild cache subsets, reduce batching window.
5) Customer-impacting support tickets (priority P0/P1) — expected 0 in first 6h; >0 triggers immediate cross-functional war room.
   - Action: escalate to SRE and product-ops, prepare targeted customer comms.
6) Billing anomaly (unexpected token burn) — detect >30% uplift compared to forecast for 1h window.
   - Action: pause non-essential background jobs, enable rate-limits for noisy keys.

Dashboard quick-views to pin (priority order):
- Live latency heatmap (per-region, per-model) with 99/95/50 pct lines
- Errors by route and by model variant
- Top 10 customer keys by qps (spot noisy clients)
- Autoscaler activity and queued requests count
- Cache hit ratio and KV store latency
- Token consumption rate vs forecast

Immediate smoke checks (T0+0–15m):
- API smoke: 20 scripted requests across routes (embed/generate/chat) — validate 200s and sample outputs
- Canary user path: run the canary flow for the cohort account list (see shared canary list)
- End-to-end: run sample customer integration tests (webhook + response verification)
- Observability sanity: tracing enabled, sample traces found for canary requests
Checklist: mark PASS/FAIL in the launch control sheet and escalate if any FAIL.

Escalation matrix (if KPIs cross critical):
- On-call SRE -> SRE lead (Ethan) -> Platform Head (vc-platform@redwood.ai)
- Product-ops command -> Exec flag if >2 regions impacted or >4 hours unresolved
- Support -> Customer Success Director if a paying customer is P0

Quick mitigation playbook (by symptom):
- Symptom: elevated latency across models
  - Check: GPU utilization, queued requests, kernel OOMs
  - Interim: shift traffic to lower-latency model variant, increase batching window, enable reserved nodes
- Symptom: sudden spike in error rate with 5xxs
  - Check: model container logs, upstream network errors, grpc timeouts
  - Interim: enable canary fallback to previous model version, disable new feature flags, rotate keys if cause is client-side spike
- Symptom: runaway token consumption from single key
  - Check: top keys table, recent account changes, automation loops
  - Interim: apply temporary rate-limit, lock key and notify account owner, investigate automation bug

Communication playbook (internal & external):
- Internal: use #launch-control Slack channel. Use structured updates every 30 minutes for first 6h (subject, current KPIs, actions taken, owner).
- Exec ping: only when an escalated threshold is hit. Use short subject line: [ESCALATION][region][impact] + 3-line summary.
- External (customer-facing): template snippets in /docs/launch-comms/templates. CS lead owns targeted messages; Comms owns public status page updates.

Runway decisions (T0+24h and T0+72h):
- T0+24h decision checkpoint: widen cohort if KPIs within warning bounds for last 3 rolling windows and <2 P1 tickets.
- T0+72h decision: full ramp if no outstanding regressions and post-launch eval shows quality parity. Document the roll decision in the rollout tracker and tag the release.

Post-launch tasks to seed the retrospective (to be completed by owners within 7 days):
- Capture incident timeline and root cause hypotheses (SRE + serving runtime)
- Cost delta report (billing team): token burn vs pre-launch forecast
- Quality drift checks: prompt/eval sample set across top 10 intents
- Customer impact log: P0/P1 ticket summaries and deliveries
- Lessons & permanent runbook updates (product-ops)

Live trackers (links + minimal fields to copy into tracker sheet):
- Launch-Control Tracker (sheet): columns = timestamp, owner, kpicycle (latency/errors/throughput), metric_value, threshold_state, action_taken, status_note, linked_jira
- Incident Triage Sheet: columns = ticket_id, owner, severity, start_time, detection_signal, root_cause_likely, mitigation, next_steps

Open questions / prework reminders (pre-launch grooming):
- Have we validated canary cohort SDK keys and webhooks? (owner: Priya)
- Are fallback model variants prepared with quantization/config differences documented? (owner: Ravi)
- Has the traffic-shift schedule been posted to regions (and are oncall windows covered)? (owner: Ethan)

Notes to self / quick scribbles (working):
- Consider temporary tighter rate limiting for trial accounts for first 48h to reduce noise.
- If cache warm-up slow, schedule a warm-up job for predicted top prefixes at T-15m.
- Confirm telemetry retention for launch traces is extended to 72h for debugging.

End of doc — use this as the tactical source for Slack updates, and paste the final snapshot into the postmortem seed file after T0+72h.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (Marisol)
- 2025-11-18: added runbook playlets and rollback triggers (Ethan + Ravi)
- 2025-11-20: communication templates and tracker links added (Sofie)
